previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: An elderly female with a history of chronic diastolic heart failure, hypertension, dementia, and chronic pain presented with worsening head, neck, chest, and abdominal pain over one week. She and her son were concerned about a possible urinary tract infection recurrence due to prior associations between infections and pain flares, though no infection was found. She was treated with acetaminophen, IV fluids, and potassium supplementation. Her elevated lactate improved with hydration, hyponatremia resolved, and supratherapeutic INR was managed by holding warfarin with follow-up instructions. Imaging showed no acute intracranial, pulmonary, or abdominal pathology. Her pain improved significantly, and she was discharged home in stable condition with plans to resume warfarin after anticoagulation clinic follow-up.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms ___ is a ___ yo woman with history of CHF (ef 55% on 
perfusion study in ___, MR and PE (on Coumadin) who presents 
with a two day history of abdominal pain and diarrhea found to 
have a UTI and hypokalemia. 
 
ACTIVE ISSUES:
# Abdominal Pain/Diarrhea due to presumed gastroenteritis- The 
patient had 3 days of pain and diarrhea with unclear trigger of 
symptoms. She was hemodynamically stable, with dry mucous 
membranes on admission that improved following IVF boluses. She 
was found to have diffuse abdominal pain, which improved 
overnight. Symptoms suggestive of a viral gastroenteritis 
(supported by mild leukopenia), however cannot exclude other 
infectious colitis. C diff, stool O+P, and stool cultures were 
ordered, but she did not have a stool for us to sample during 
this hospitalization. CT was not concerning for acute processes 
including diverticulitis or obstruction. Patient was previously 
on colchicine for a gout flare but it does not appear that she 
is still on this medication. She was found to have a UTI, which 
may also have contributed to her discomfort as pain did localize 
to some extent to the lower abdomen. In the morning after her 
admission following IVF, her pain had improved with no further 
loose stools. Her diet was advanced, and she tolerated a regular 
diet with no nausea. 

# Bacterial UTI- UA was consistent with UTI, no CVA pain to 
suggest pyelonephritis. She endorsed dysuria, but no urinary 
frequency or urgency. She was started on CTX, but as she 
appeared non-toxic and was able tolerate PO, she was switched to 
Cipro. She has a history of Klebsiella UTIs, sensitive to Cipro. 
 Urine culture are still pending.  Continue Cipro for 3 days 
(through ___

# Hypokalemia- Her initial K was 2.6 in the ED. No EKG changes 
were seen. We suspect this is related to her diarrhea and poor 
PO intake. She received a total of K 140meq by IV and PO to 
replete, and her K was 3.7 on the morning of discharge. Her 
Furosemide was held during this hospitalization. 

# Hyponatremia- Patient has a history of mild hyponatremia in 
the setting of poor PO intake. She had Na of 129 in the ED, 
corrected with IVF bolus. 
 
# Leukopenia- ___ be related to bone marrow suppression in the 
setting of a viral  infection. Differential was normal.  

# Anemia- She has a history of microcytic anemia, but appears to 
have had macrocytosis since ___. HCT down from baseline of 34 
to 31 on admission. There were no signs of active bleeding and 
guaiac was negative in the ED. Drop overnight from 31 to 27.7 
likely dilutional due to IVF bolus. Defer to outpatient work up 
for chronic anemia. 

# Anticoagulation for DVT/PEs- She is on Coumadin 2mg daily and 
came in with INR 2.9. Gave half dose at 1mg given high INR and 
in anticipation of potentiation with concurrent antibiotic 
treatment. 

# Chart history of chronic diastolic CHF - Preserved EF on Echo 
___. Appeared hypovolemic on exam and improved with IVF and PO 
intake. Chest imaging more consistent with atelectasis and 
potential interstitial disease, rather than vascular congestion. 
Atelectasis likely splinting from recent abdominal pain. She was 
continued on her home metoprolol, and Lasix was held. 

CHRONIC DIAGNOSES
# HTN- She was normotensive during her stay and was continued on 
her home metoprolol.  
# GERD- continued home pantoprazole

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ female with symptoms concerning for ischemic colitis.
Rule out ischemic colitis.

COMPARISONS:  CT abdomen and pelvis from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT axial imaging was obtained from the lung bases through the
pubic symphysis following the administration of intravenous contrast material.
Coronal and sagittal reformats were completed.

DLP:  635.6 mGy-cm.

FINDINGS:

CT ABDOMEN WITH CONTRAST:  There is a 3-mm nodule in the right lower lobe,
unchanged from prior study in ___.  Bibasilar atelectasis is
present.  The heart is top normal in size without any pericardial effusion. 
The liver enhances homogenously without any focal lesions or intra- or
extra-hepatic biliary dilatation.  The portal vein is patent.  The
gallbladder, pancreas, spleen, and adrenal glands are unremarkable.  Aside
from a tiny hypodensity in the upper pole of the left kidney, which is too
small to characterize, there are no other focal lesions or hydronephrosis. 
The stomach, small and intra-abdominal large bowel are unremarkable and
nonobstructed.  There is no free fluid, free air or lymphadenopathy within the
abdomen.  The aorta is of normal caliber without evidence of aneurysm.  There
is minimal atherosclerotic calcification and the major branches are patent.

CT PELVIS:  There is sigmoid diverticulosis extending up into the descending
colon, but no evidence of diverticulitis.  There is no free fluid, free air or
lymphadenopathy within the pelvis.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  Again seen is S-shaped scoliosis of the spine and
degenerative changes.  A left hip replacement is noted.  There are no
concerning osseous lesions.

IMPRESSION:  Extensive diverticulosis without evidence of diverticulitis. No
acute process.

CHEST RADIOGRAPH PERFORMED ON ___

COMPARISON:  Prior exam from ___.

CLINICAL HISTORY:  Bibasilar rales and dropping sats.

FINDINGS:  AP upright and lateral views of the chest were provided. 
Comparison is also made with same date CT abdomen and pelvis.  There is mild
bibasilar atelectasis.  Coarsened reticular markings could reflect chronic
interstitial disease.  The possibility of mild pulmonary interstitial edema is
not excluded.  No large effusion or pneumothorax.  The heart and mediastinal
contour is stable.  Bony structures are intact.

IMPRESSION:  Bibasilar atelectasis, mild interstitial coarsening, which could
represent interstitial lung disease or possibly mild interstitial edema.
